sections.content: If you are searching for real estate deals in Evansville IN, you have landed on a market that most coastal investors are still sleeping on. Evansville sits in the southwest corner of Indiana along the Ohio River, and it quietly checks almost every box serious investors look for: low home prices, steady rental demand, a diversified local economy, and room for appreciation. Whether you are a first-time investor just getting started with our [Real Estate Investing for Beginners](aiwholesail.com/guides/real-estate-investing-for-beginners) guide, or a seasoned wholesaler looking to expand into new markets, Evansville deserves a serious look in 2024.
Evansville IN Market Overview: Why Investors Are Paying Attention

Evansville is the third-largest city in Indiana with a population of around 117,000 people. The metro area, which includes Vanderburgh, Warrick, and Gibson counties, pushes that number closer to 315,000. The city's economy is anchored by healthcare (Ascension St. Vincent and Deaconess Health System are major employers), manufacturing, retail, and higher education through the University of Southern Indiana and University of Evansville. This diverse employer base keeps unemployment relatively low and rental demand consistent year over year. Median household income sits around $48,000, which is below the national average — and that is actually good news for investors. It means there is a large pool of renters who either cannot or choose not to buy, creating stable occupancy rates for buy-and-hold landlords. You can explore current market data and active deal flow on our [Evansville IN market page](aiwholesail.com/markets/evansville-in).
Average Home Prices in Evansville IN

One of the biggest draws for investors is how affordable Evansville remains compared to national averages. As of 2024, the median home price in Evansville is approximately $165,000 to $175,000, well below the national median of around $420,000. Entry-level properties in working-class neighborhoods can be found in the $80,000 to $120,000 range, while renovated homes in desirable areas command $200,000 to $280,000. This wide pricing spread creates opportunities at every level — from low-cost wholesale deals to mid-range flips targeting move-up buyers. After-repair values (ARVs) on fully renovated 3-bedroom, 2-bath homes in strong neighborhoods typically land between $175,000 and $240,000, giving flippers meaningful profit margin when deals are sourced correctly.

Before you run the numbers on any Evansville deal, use the free [ARV Calculator at aiwholesail.com/tools/arv-calculator](aiwholesail.com/tools/arv-calculator) to quickly estimate after-repair value based on comparable sales. Getting your ARV right before you make an offer is the single most important step in avoiding a bad deal.
Best Neighborhoods for Real Estate Investors in Evansville
Not all Evansville zip codes are created equal. Knowing where to focus your energy saves time and protects your capital. Here is a breakdown of the most investor-friendly areas:
East Side: The Safest Bet for Landlords and Flippers

The East Side of Evansville, including areas around the 47715 and 47725 zip codes, is where most owner-occupant buyers and young families want to live. Home values are stronger here, turnover is lower, and tenant quality tends to be higher. Flippers targeting the retail buyer market will find their best exit strategy on the East Side. Expect to pay more for your entry price — distressed properties here often start at $100,000 to $130,000 even before renovation — but ARVs in the $200,000 to $250,000 range make the math work on the right deals.
West Side and Downtown: High-Yield Rental Territory

The West Side and areas near downtown Evansville offer some of the highest gross rental yields in the market, often 10% to 14% on properly purchased properties. Home prices here are lower — you can find 3-bedroom rentals in the $60,000 to $100,000 range — and monthly rents of $700 to $950 are achievable. The trade-off is higher management intensity and occasional vacancy challenges. Investors who use professional property managers and vet tenants carefully can build strong cash-flowing portfolios in these zip codes. The 47712 and 47713 zip codes are worth your attention.
Newburgh and Warrick County: Suburban Growth Corridor

Just east of Evansville in Warrick County, the town of Newburgh has seen steady population growth as families move out of the city for better schools and newer housing. Median prices here run $220,000 to $300,000, making it less attractive for traditional wholesale deals but excellent for new construction investing or targeting move-up buyers on mid-range flips. If you are building a long-term rental portfolio, Newburgh offers appreciation potential that core Evansville neighborhoods cannot match.
Types of Real Estate Deals Available in Evansville IN

items: Wholesale Deals: Evansville has an active wholesale market with motivated sellers including probate estates, tax-delinquent owners, and absentee landlords with deferred-maintenance properties. Assignment fees of $5,000 to $20,000 are common on well-priced deals. Read our complete guide on [Wholesaling Real Estate for Beginners](aiwholesail.com/guides/wholesaling-real-estate-for-beginners) to learn the step-by-step process.

Fix and Flip: The flip market is solid for investors who can source deals below $100,000 and target ARVs in the $175,000 to $230,000 range. Renovation costs in Evansville average $25 to $40 per square foot for mid-grade rehabs, which is notably lower than national averages due to affordable local labor.

Buy-and-Hold Rentals: Single-family rentals in the $80,000 to $130,000 price range commonly rent for $750 to $1,100 per month, producing cash-on-cash returns of 8% to 12% for investors who buy right. Small multifamily properties (duplexes and fourplexes) are also available and can accelerate portfolio growth.

BRRRR Strategy: The Buy, Rehab, Rent, Refinance, Repeat strategy works well in Evansville because acquisition costs are low and properties can be refinanced at significantly higher values post-renovation, allowing investors to pull most of their capital back out.

Tax Lien and Tax Deed Investing: Indiana holds annual tax sales, and Vanderburgh County regularly offers tax-delinquent properties at courthouse auctions. These can be excellent entry points for investors willing to navigate the legal process.

sections.content: Evansville Real Estate Market Trends to Watch in 2024

Several trends are shaping the Evansville market right now. First, inventory remains tight. The number of active listings in Vanderburgh County has stayed well below pre-pandemic norms, which is keeping prices supported even as higher interest rates cool buyer demand nationally. Second, rent growth has been modest but consistent, averaging 3% to 5% annually over the past three years. Third, the Ford Motor Company's decision to invest in electric vehicle battery production at nearby facilities has created jobs and economic optimism across the tri-state area. Finally, downtown Evansville has seen renewed investment in mixed-use developments and renovated historic buildings, which is gradually improving the near-downtown neighborhood comps.

The best real estate markets for investors are not the ones everyone is already talking about — they are the stable, affordable Midwestern cities where the numbers actually work. Evansville is exactly that kind of market.
How to Find Off-Market Deals in Evansville

The most profitable real estate deals in Evansville IN rarely show up on the MLS at investor-friendly prices. To find the best opportunities, you need to go off-market. Direct mail campaigns targeting absentee owners, probate attorneys, and tax-delinquent property lists are proven approaches in this market. Driving for dollars in the West Side and older residential pockets can surface distressed properties before they hit anyone's radar. Building relationships with local wholesalers who already work the market is another fast path to deal flow. For a full breakdown of off-market strategies, see our detailed guide on [How to Find Off-Market Real Estate Deals](aiwholesail.com/guides/off-market-real-estate-deals).
Tips for Out-of-State Investors Targeting Evansville

Evansville is attracting more out-of-state investors every year, particularly from high-cost markets in California, Illinois, and the Pacific Northwest where the same dollars buy much less. If you are investing remotely, here is what you need to know:

items: Build your team first: Find a local real estate agent who works with investors, a reliable property manager (expect 8% to 10% of monthly rent), a licensed contractor who can provide accurate rehab bids, and a local real estate attorney.

Visit at least once before your first purchase: A single market visit will teach you more about neighborhood quality than hours of online research. Drive the streets, visit properties, and meet your team in person.
Understand Indiana landlord-tenant law: Indiana is generally considered a landlord-friendly state with reasonable eviction timelines, but you should know the rules before your first tenant dispute.

Use technology to analyze deals remotely: Tools like the free [Wholesale Deal Calculator at aiwholesail.com/tools/wholesale-deal-calculator](aiwholesail.com/tools/wholesale-deal-calculator) let you run numbers on deals from anywhere in seconds.

Join local real estate investor associations: The Southwest Indiana Real Estate Investors Association (SWIREIA) hosts regular meetings and is a great place to find local partners, contractors, and deal flow.

Verify comps carefully: Evansville neighborhoods can change block by block. Always confirm your ARV and rental comps with a local agent or appraiser who knows the specific area, not just the zip code.

sections.content: Once you have identified a potential deal, use our guide on [How to Analyze Real Estate Deals Like a Pro](aiwholesail.com/guides/how-to-analyze-real-estate-deals) to stress-test your numbers before submitting an offer. Run three scenarios — conservative, base case, and optimistic — to make sure the deal holds up even if renovation costs come in higher than expected.
Is Evansville IN Right for Your Investment Strategy?

Evansville is not a market that will make you rich overnight. It is not a high-appreciation coastal market, and it will not double in value in three years. What it will do is produce consistent, predictable returns for investors who buy right, manage carefully, and play the long game. For cash flow investors, the numbers are hard to beat at current price levels. For flippers, the spread between distressed prices and retail ARVs is wide enough to generate solid profits on well-managed projects. And for wholesalers, there is enough motivated seller inventory to build a real business here without facing the cutthroat competition you find in bigger metro areas. The investors who will win in this market are the ones who do the work to understand it deeply — and who move quickly when good deals surface.
